'''''Oscularia deltoides''''', the '''deltoid-leaved dewplant''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''''dassievygie''''' or '''''sandsteenvygie''''' is a [[species]] of flowering [[succulent plant|succulent]] plant in the fig-marigold [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Aizoaceae that is [[native plant|native]] to the [[Western Cape|south-western Cape]], South Africa.<ref>{{cite web |title=''Oscularia deltoides'' |url=http://pza.sanbi.org/oscularia-deltoides |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214060908/http://pza.sanbi.org/oscularia-deltoides |archive-date=2021-12-14 |access-date=23 July 2013 |work= |publisher=SA National Biodiversity Institute}}</ref>

==Description==
This intensely flowering plant is found growing among [[sandstone]] rocks in the winter-rainfall mountains of the far south-western corner of South Africa. Growing to {{convert|30|cm|0|abbr=on}} high and spreading indefinitely,<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|page=1136}}</ref> it has silver-blue foliage. The fat, succulent leaves are three-sided (hence the qualifier ''deltoides'' – "triangular"),<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=9781845337315|page=224}}</ref> with red teeth on the margins. The stems are often tinged purple.

In the spring it produces masses of pink, almond-scented flowers.

==Cultivation==
It is increasingly grown in South African gardens as an ornamental plant and can easily be propagated from cuttings, which should be planted in a sunny position. This low-maintenance succulent spreads out forming a colourful mat and grows well on the rocky edge of flower beds where it cascades over the edge. It attracts butterflies. In colder [[temperateness|temperate]] regions it requires winter protection or glass cover. It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=''Oscularia deltoides''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/11979/Oscularia-deltoides/Details|publisher=Royal Horticultural Society|access-date=18 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 70 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 14 April 2018}}</ref> 

It was previously classed in the genus ''[[Lampranthus]]'', as ''Lampranthus deltoides''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Oscularia deltoides|url=http://fernkloof.com/species2.mv?Oscularia%20deltoides|publisher=Fernkloof Nature Reserve|access-date=23 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120308092329/http://fernkloof.com/species2.mv?Oscularia%20deltoides|archive-date=8 March 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>
